example_raw:
Isn't it great? (Switzerland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; German; Pass)

Don't you like pizza? (Burmese, A2 WAYSTAGE)

[Talking about a car] I bought one. Didn't I tell you? (Portuguese, A2 WAYSTAGE)

positives: Isn't it a wonderful day?
Don't you want to come?
negatives: He isn't here right now.
Wouldn't it be wonderful!

example_raw:
Why don't we watch a film? (Sri Lanka; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

Why didn't you come with me? (Bulgaria; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Bulgarian; Pass)

Why don't you ask Jennifer to go with you? (Uruguay; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Why couldn't you come? It was fun. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Suggesting actions or asking for reasons.

positives: Why don't we go to the park?
What couldn't you understand?
negatives: I don't know why he isn't here.
Tell me what didn't work.

example_raw:
What a pity that you didn't come. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

What a pity you lost the information about the new art class. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expressing regret or disappointment over a situation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'what a pity' followed by a clause to express feelings.

positives: What a pity that you couldn't make it.
What a pity it rained all day.
negatives: It's a pity.
She felt pity for the poor dog.

can_do_statement: Can use 'What a' + noun phrase and 'What a' + noun phrase + clause.
example_raw:
What a brilliant idea. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; French; Pass)

What a nice present I have! (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

What a great afternoon I had yesterday! (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; French; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expressing strong emotion or surprise about a noun.

positives: What a brilliant idea!
What a nice surprise.
negatives: I don't know what a dog is.
What a pity you couldn't stay.

example_raw:
How exciting! (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Chinese; Pass)

How terrible! (Bosnia-Herzegovina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Serbian; Pass)

How amazing! This is my first flight in a hot-air balloon. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expressing an intense emotional reaction to a situation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'how' with an adjective for exclamation.

positives: How wonderful!
How strange.
negatives: How are you?
I don't know how fast he was going.

example_raw:
How lucky you are to have visited that exhibition! (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; French; Pass)

How lovely to get your letter. (Iran; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Farsi; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expressing feeling regarding an entire clause.

positives: How lucky you are to have visited that exhibition!
How lovely to get your letter.
negatives: How exciting!
How do you do that?

can_do_statement: Can use the negative interrogative form of an auxiliary verb to express surprise or enthusiasm.
example_raw:
Wouldn't it be wonderful! (Russian, B2 VANTAGE)

Doesn't that sound excellent to you?! (Denmark; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Danish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Using a negative question format to express positive enthusiasm or surprise.

positives: Wouldn't it be wonderful!
Doesn't that sound excellent to you?!
negatives: He isn't here.
Isn't it a wonderful day?

example_raw:
How I often longed to play with the other children or relax with a good book. (Germany; C2 MASTERY; 1993; German; Pass)

How I love the smell of home! (Brazil; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

How I long to be there again. (Netherlands; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Dutch; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'How' directly followed by a subject and verb.

positives: How I love the smell of home!
How she wishes things were different.
negatives: How are you?
How exciting!

example_raw: How differently we were brought up by our mother. (Germany; C2 MASTERY; 1993; German; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing the manner of an action.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'How' + adverb to start an exclamation.

positives: How beautifully she sang.
How differently we were brought up.
negatives: How I love that.
How exciting!

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'who' as the subject.
example_raw:
It's about a girl who went to the war when she was 22 years old. (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I'd like a pen-friend who really likes music and reading. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

I can tell you that I agree with people who think that Stonehenge is magic place. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Polish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Identifying a specific person within a group.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'who' as the subject in a defining relative clause.

positives: I need a friend who really listens to me.
The man who is standing there is my brother.
negatives: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
I don't know who did it.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'which' as the subject.
example_raw:
At the end of the game, the KASAS sang to Hagas a piece of music which makes me cry. Suzanna watched with me and she cried alot. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

You should wear clothes which can get dirty. (Switzerland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Swiss German; Pass)

I bought a t-shirt which has a picture of a car on it and I bought a shirt for my brother. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Turkish; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' as the subject in a defining relative clause.

positives: I want a car which runs fast.
He read a book which changed his life.
negatives: The house, which is red, is nice.
I don't know which to choose.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'that' as the object.
example_raw:
The team that I like is called 'The Monkeys', but Paty prefers 'The Walls'. (Uruguay; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I bought some clothes that I will need for my trip to Greece. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Greek; Pass)

Please, wear clothes that you can get dirty; use old clothes, okay? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Providing more info about a noun by acting as the object of a relative clause.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'that' as the object in a defining relative clause.

positives: The team that I like won.
I bought clothes that I need.
negatives: I know that he is here.
That is my car.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'who' as the subject.
example_raw:
I watched it with my brother who was also interested in sports. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Chinese; Pass)

It's given by Jenny who is one of my best friends. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

I want my mobile before this afternoon because my parents who are in Japan will call me. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Tamil; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Adding extra, non-essential information about a person.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'who' in a non-defining relative clause.

positives: My brother, who is a doctor, lives in London.
I saw Mary, who was walking her dog.
negatives: The man who is standing there is my brother.
I don't know who did it.

can_do_statement: Can use a non-defining relative clause with 'which' as the subject,.
example_raw:
I bought it in Peter's Mobile shop, which is near to my home. (Sri Lanka; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Tamil; Pass)

I've been to Cardiff which is the capital city of Wales. (Korea, South; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Korean; Pass)

I visited a museum and an exhibition which were really excellent. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

I bought two shirts, which cost £20 and four sweatshirts, which were a little expensive. (KET; A2 WAYSTAGE; Pass; 2008)

The mobile phone is green, which is my favourite colour. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Turkish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Adding extra, non-essential information about a thing.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' in a non-defining relative clause.

positives: My car, which is red, is very fast.
I read that book, which was very interesting.
negatives: The car which I bought is red.
I don't know which to choose.

can_do_statement: Can use a defining relative clause with 'which' as the object.
example_raw:
I came to your house yesterday with the computer game which I borrowed from Mayank. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Hindi; Pass)

The coffee-cup which my good friend gave me is pretty. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

Sorry, I can't do anything to help because I will try again to pass an exam which I failed last year. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

The colour which I prefer is pink, so we will use pink. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Bihari; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Identifying a specific thing as the object.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'which' as the object in a defining relative clause.

positives: The computer game which I borrowed is great.
The colour which I prefer is pink.
negatives: The game, which I borrowed, is great.
I don't know which game you mean.
